inline.s: [Haō (a stylistic name)]
It refers to an additional appellation a person takes apart from his given name and courtesy name. For example: “Li Bai, courtesy name Taibai, style name the Hermit of the Green Lotus.”

[Dingkai asked about the purport of the three contemplations in a single mind. The Bodhisattva said: “The three contemplations of the Tiantai school have their wonder in the center of the mind. If one knows the center of the mind, the way is entirely realized.” He had [Dingkai] stand with Dingmian
(Zikai)
side by side
(he had him stand shoulder to shoulder with Dingmian)
, and gave a gatha: “One opening and a second opening, today you come again; the bodhi has its seed, and a wondrous hand plants both.”]

Dingkai asked about the purport of the three contemplations in a single mind, and the Bodhisattva said: “The three contemplations of the Tiantai school have their wonder in the center of the mind. If one knows the center of the mind, the three contemplations in a single mind will be completely understood.” Then the Bodhisattva had him stand side by side with Dingmian (Zikai) and gave a gatha: “Dingkai and Zikai, today you come again; the bodhi naturally has its seed, and a wondrous hand nurtures both.”

[The three contemplations in a single mind (yixin sanguan)] The contemplation method of the Tiantai school. The Tiantai school says that the entire universe of existences all possess the three truths of emptiness, provisionality, and the middle, and that these three truths are mutually present and mutually fused: emptiness is provision and middle, provision is emptiness and middle, and the middle is emptiness and provision. If we contemplate in this way within a single mind, it is called “the three contemplations in a single mind.” [The three truths (sandi)] The truth of emptiness, the truth of provisionality, and the truth of the middle. The truth of emptiness means that things are empty of self-substance; the truth of provisionality means that there are merely provisional, condition-arisen appearances; the truth of the middle means that all dharmas are neither empty nor provisional yet both empty and provisional — the real principle of the Middle Way. These three truths were established by the Tiantai school.

[Instructing Shande, he said: “Your head is already shaved; you should know contentment. Think on impermanence and cut off love and desire. Namo Amitābha — thought after thought, constantly in succession.”]

He instructed Shande: “Your head is already shaved (aged and weakened in strength); you should know contentment. Think on impermanence and cut off love and desire. Namo Amitābha — thought after thought, constantly in succession.”

[Instructing Erzhi, he said: “Diligence keeps one from illness; without diligence, illness comes. Do not say that past karma will be repaid only very far off. The compassionate father Amitābha — visit him again and again; this can prolong your years, and how much more dispel illness.”]

He instructed Erzhi: “Diligence keeps one from illness; without diligence, illness comes. Do not say that past karma's recompense is very far off. The compassionate father Amitābha — visit him again and again (constantly); this can bring long life and can also remove sickness and pain.”

[Instructing Chen Daxin, he said: “Growing old without letting go, at death you will surely be entangled. When the debt to children and family is repaid, then you may be happy. The Western Land of Ultimate Bliss is not far; do not cut yourself off from it.”]

He instructed Chen Daxin: “Growing old without letting go (at an age still not shedding one's entanglements), at death you will surely be entangled (at death you will certainly be burdened by them). When the debt to children and family is repaid, then you may be happy. The Western Land of Ultimate Bliss is not far; do not cut yourself off from it.”

[Instructing Shen Yuanhui, he said: “Dwelling deep and hidden without showing oneself — this is called upholding the precepts. If one floats to the surface and out, before long one will surely fail. Since the thought is not true, one cannot be free; fortune and misfortune, good and ill — you yourself make them strange.”]

He instructed Shen Yuanhui: “Dwelling deep and hidden without showing oneself — this is called upholding the precepts. If one floats to the surface and out, before long one will surely fail. Since the thought is not true, one cannot be free; fortune and misfortune, good and ill — you yourself make them strange (fortune and misfortune have no door; only people call them upon themselves).”

[Instructing Du Yijian, he said: “The good is righteousness; the not-good is not righteousness. Righteousness and good are not two; what is seen is only righteousness. Taking righteousness as one's view, one does not see the not-righteous. When one sees the not-righteous, then seeing has nothing to see that is righteous.”]

He instructed Du Yijian: “The good is righteousness; the not-good is then not righteousness. Righteousness and good are not two; what is seen is only righteousness. Taking righteousness as one's view, one does not see the not-righteous; taking the not-righteous as one's view, one does not see righteousness.”
[Righteousness (yi)]
The principle or action that is just and fitting.
[Instructing the female disciple Yian, he said: “Is it because of illness that you do not recite the Buddha? Ah
yī
, an exclamation)
! The more severe the illness, the more diligent the recitation should be. If one lets the illness reach the point where one cannot recite, then one has erred indeed.”]

He instructed the female disciple Yian: “Is it because you are ill that you do not recite the Buddha? Ah! The more serious the illness, the more diligent the recitation should be. If you let the illness reach the point where you cannot recite, then you have erred indeed.”
[Instructing Wuxiu, he said: “Is a foot-long jade disk a treasure? The inch of time should be treasured. Think rightly on Amitābha — the light of faith is brilliant
(resplendent and shining)
. Do not cling to former acquaintances, or the road ahead will be forever lost.”]

He instructed Wuxiu: “A foot-long jade disk is not really precious; the inch of time is precious and should be cherished. Think rightly on Amitābha, and the light of faith shines brilliantly. Do not cling to the friends of old acquaintance, lest the practice of the Way be lost forever.”
[A foot-long jade disk (chibi)] A jade disk one foot in diameter. [An inch of time (cunyin)] A brief span of time. The Huainanzi
in the chapter “Tracing the Way” says: “The sage does not prize a foot of jade, but values an inch of time, because time is hard to get and easy to lose.”
[Instructing Changshe, he said: “Having a mouth, yet as if dumb; having ears, yet as if deaf. Break with the crowd and leave the world, and the Way is then exalted.”]

He instructed Changshe: “Having a mouth, yet as if dumb; having ears, yet as if deaf. Break with the crowd and leave the world, and the Way is then exalted (only when the practice of the Way is accomplished can it be grand).”
[Instructing Changyuan, he said: “Let your conduct not be negligent; negligence is not that of a bhikṣu. Those who ruin themselves have many sorrows after death.”]
He instructed Changyuan: “Your cultivation must not be negligent; negligence is not that of a bhikṣu. Those who ruin their own practice of the Way will have great troubles afterward.”
[Instructing Dingmao, he said: “You are one of the Way; you should purify your mind. Those who can purify the mind can transcend the multitude.”]
He instructed Dingmao: “You are one of the Way (you are a cultivator of the Way); you should purify your mind. Those who can purify the mind can transcend the multitude.”

[Instructing Dingsui, he said: “Honesty is a treasure, yet it also has its shortcoming: if one is only this, it merely suffices for food and warmth. What is the use of leaving home? Wish to be free of delusion and affliction; you should give rise to the mind of the Way, and not let the time pass in vain.”]

He instructed Dingsui: “Honesty is a treasure, yet it also has its shortcoming: if one is merely this, it only suffices for food and warmth. What is the use of leaving home? Wish to be free of afflictions such as greed, anger, and delusion; you should give rise to the mind of the Way, and not let the time pass in vain.”
[Instructing Zha Dinghong, he said: “The Bodhisattva's gatha is like the everyday tea and rice. Go back and tell your mother: the matter of her own [rebirth] should be attended to early.”]

He instructed Zha Dinghong: “The Bodhisattva's gatha is like everyday tea and rice. Go back and tell your mother: the great matter of being reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss must be attended to early.”
[Go back and tell your mother: attend to your own matter early]
The Bodhisattva's instruction to Zha Dinghong's mother is found in the section “Wrong Views Lead the Way Astray.”
[Instructing Chen Dingzhuan, he said: “Only Heaven is highest, and it sees everything. Guard your first mind — take care that it changes not even a little.”]
He instructed Chen Dingzhuan: “Only Heaven is highest and sees everything. You must protect your first mind and be very careful not to let it retreat.”
[Instructing Daben, he said: “To reach the root is to be without root; all conditions should be stilled. Why do you not dwell in peace, and are still bustling
jíjí
? One day you will let go; then the man farms and the woman weaves. Reflecting on your former life, you will weep alone.”]

He instructed Daben: “To reach the root is to be without root (the world is an illusion); all conditions should be stilled (all conditions are impermanent). Why do you not cultivate with a still mind, but still eagerly pursue outward with all your might? Once life ends, the next life is again the wheel of rebirth; reflecting on your former life of no effort, you have only regret and tears.”

[One day you will let go; then the man farms and the woman weaves] Once life ends, the next life is again the man farming and the woman weaving (a metaphor that if in this life one has not realized the Way, in the next life one is still within the wheel of rebirth).

[Then, when the Bodhisattva had instructed each one, he said again to them: “Since I have descended here, all my words are the essential wonders of practice. If you can contemplate them at all times and earnestly follow them, you will surely be born in the highest grade. The Bodhisattva will from now on come no more. You disciples should each exert yourselves, and do not make this assembly vain.”]

Then, when the Bodhisattva had instructed each one, he said again to the assembly: “Since I have descended to this place, all my words are the essential wonders of practice. If you can contemplate them at all times and earnestly follow them, you will certainly be reborn in the highest grade. The Bodhisattva will from now on come no more. You disciples should each exert yourselves, and not have attended this assembly in vain.”

[Then, hearing the Bodhisattva's words, the disciples all wept in sorrowful attachment and could not raise their eyes. The Bodhisattva said to them: “Disciples, you think that because the Bodhisattva will not descend again, you might grow negligent and from then on lose your footing. But in truth it is not so. Why? From now on, your vigor is only your own vigor; leaving the dusty path
(the same as the world of dust)

and ascending to the realm of sages — this is the doing of the greatly wise and the greatly worthy. If you are negligent, that too is your own negligence; turning your back on the great Way and entering the mud — this is the doing of the ignorant and the foolish. Disciples, you have only to go forward and not give rise to attachment; only press on with effort, and there is no need for sorrow.”]

Then, hearing the Bodhisattva say this, the disciples all wept in sorrowful attachment and could not raise their eyes. The Bodhisattva said to them: “Disciples, because the Bodhisattva will not descend again, you fear that you might grow negligent and from then on lose your footing. But in truth it is not so. Why? From now on, your vigor is your own vigor (vigor depends on yourself); leaving the Saha world and ascending to Ultimate Bliss — this is the doing of the greatly wise and the greatly worthy. If you are negligent, that too is your own negligence (negligence also depends on yourself); turning your back on the great Way and entering the mud — this is the doing of the ignorant and the foolish. Disciples, you have only to press forward and not give rise to attachment; only press on with urgent effort, and there is no need for sorrow.”

[After a while, he again admonished: “You must not again entertain the thought that the Bodhisattva will descend. Why? The establishment of the phoenix planchette is originally that on which spirits and ghosts rely; it is not the constant work of the great Bodhisattva's manifestation. If you follow the teaching without fail, and give rise toward the Bodhisattva a mind of reverence and the thought of [an encounter] hard to obtain
(the thought of something extremely hard to encounter)
, that is the great place of repaying kindness.”]

After a while, the Bodhisattva again instructed: “You must not again entertain the thought that the Bodhisattva will descend. Why? The planchette is originally what spirits and ghosts rely upon; this is not the constant work of the great Bodhisattva's manifestation. If you follow the teaching without fail, and give rise toward the Bodhisattva a mind of reverence and the thought of something extremely hard to encounter, that is the great place of repaying kindness.”

[At that time, although the disciples heard the Dharma admonition, they still gathered around, unwilling to disperse. The Bodhisattva again admonished: “Disciples, in his past causal practice the Bodhisattva had a great connection with you. Although he will not descend again from now on, you must not entertain the thought of [his being] far away. You should know that the Enlightened, Bright, Wondrous Practice [Bodhisattva] is at all times before your eyes, following you without leaving. Take care that you do not for a single day become lax, and thereby abandon the Enlightened Bright Wondrous Practice yourselves.”]

At that time, although the disciples heard the Bodhisattva's Dharma admonition, they still gathered around, unwilling to disperse. The Bodhisattva again instructed: “Disciples, in his past causal practice the Bodhisattva had a great connection with you. Although he will not descend again from now on, you must not entertain the thought of the Bodhisattva's being far away. You should know that the Enlightened, Bright, Wondrous Practice [Bodhisattva] is at all times before your eyes, following you without leaving. Take care that you do not for a single day become indolent, or else you yourselves abandon the Enlightened Bright Wondrous Practice!”

[After a little while, he again admonished: “Disciples, since the Dharma assembly is finished, you should each disperse. The Bodhisattva comes without origin and goes without destination. Do not only sit staring and guarding; the Bodhisattva is surely not on a sheet of paper. Let each of you recite one ‘Namo Amitābha Buddha,’ make salutation with utmost sincerity, and receive
(reverently receive)
and put it into practice — that is enough.”]

After a little while, the Bodhisattva again instructed: “Disciples, since the Dharma assembly is already ended, everyone should disperse. The Bodhisattva comes without origin and goes without destination. Do not only sit staring and guarding; the Bodhisattva is after all not on this sheet of paper of the planchette (this means: one should guard the Enlightened Bright Wondrous Practice Bodhisattva in the mind, not guard the Enlightened Bright Wondrous Practice Bodhisattva on the planchette paper). Let each of you recite one ‘Namo Amitābha Buddha,’ make salutation with utmost sincerity, reverently receive my instruction, and earnestly put it into practice — that is enough.”
Reliable Pointers to the Western Land (End)
